rv.q: We are told Khan wrote fiction but not much more. A character likens storytellers to spies but the play lacks the essential conflict and suspense of either. Burford’s performance is solid but workmanlike.
Biographical wartime drama reverently relates the story of British intelligence agent Noor Inayat Khan

The script by Stephanie Street, rightly focuses deeply on Noor, her anxieties, the pressure she puts herself under and how her direct relationships with her family and colleagues impact her decisions.

Bringing the story to life is an all-female cast, lead by Priyanga Burford as Noor-un-Nisa, rarely ever leaving the stage. Burford does a fine job of portraying our protagonist, but feels let down by the script and direction, often leaving the role feeling hollow.
